2026

AfterglowNovember, 2026

Phone VR, done properly. A native XR platform that turns an iPhone in a printable viewer into a real headset: 6DoF head tracking from ARKit, stereo passthrough laid over the LiDAR depth so the room has its own depth, hand tracking on the Neural Engine, and a glass window interface that hangs in your room. A WebKit browser with a custom WebXR layer gives pages your hands, immersive VR and AR sessions, and hit tests against your real surfaces. Spatial photos and video play in stereo, 360 photos become the room, and twelve games with lit 3D graphics run around you, from mini golf at your feet to a coaster on a new course every ride. Rewritten from a Unity prototype into Swift 6 and Metal with single-pass stereo, tuned to hold its frame rate on a phone. Free and open source (Apache-2.0).

ShepherdOctober, 2026

A self-hosted guardian for your home network: DNS filtering against a 95-list catalog, per-device/group/network policy with allowlist mode and scheduled access, a live 3D globe HUD of every query with replay, automatic device naming and classification, an alarm engine, port and vulnerability scanning, and geo-IP country blocking, behind a locked portal with a trusted-browser PIN. One native binary for Linux, macOS and Windows — no cloud, no telemetry, no account. Free and open source under the AGPL. Try the real portal UI with synthetic data right on the site.

TomSeptember, 2026

A music machine that runs entirely in your browser, and on the command line. Dial in a melody in seconds — style, key, tempo, swing, shape — or snap a whole song together from blocks like Lego, and let Auto build, finish or re-roll whatever you haven't locked. Every note comes from a seed, so the same seed always makes the same music, and because Tom writes all of it, it's royalty-free: no samples, no licenses, no Content ID claims. Exports WAV, MIDI and JSON, and a share link's hashtag is the whole song. Free and open source under MIT.

LatheSeptember, 2026

An open-source media engine for Apple platforms, and a free Mac app built on it. The Swift package encodes, converts, tags and recovers media entirely on the device — HEIC, AVIF, WebP, HEVC, AV1 and MP3, chapters and subtitles, Flash movies — through the system frameworks, with no subprocesses, so the same code runs on an iPhone. Tri-AddMay, 2014

Some ideas you have to talk about when saying goodbye to a great friend. This was the concept for Tri-Add, named by my friend’s mother. Simply an additive color mixing game that turned out to be not so simple. This was our first go at an original game, and it played with simple sound effects and animation. The premise seems simple, but it got progressively more difficult as you went through the theoretically limitless randomized levels. This app was built when Obj-C was the only language on iOS. Relaunched in 2026 — rebuilt from scratch in Swift 6 / SwiftUI with liquid-glass color mixing, additive & subtractive modes, inversion stages, Game Center, an iMessage extension, and an Apple Watch app.
